solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Child brings home some works of Shakespeare (7)

blocks.note: a son is a child
to net is to bring home, as in netting a profit

annotation.surface: A child comes home from school carrying a few volumes of Shakespeare.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brings home' reads as carrying something into the house; here it means earns, as a salary nets a sum.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Shakespeare wrote 154 fourteen-line poems of this kind, a small part of his output.

entries.clue: Rest matters when dancing for savvy American (6-5)

indicatorNotes.when dancing: dancers move about the floor and change places, so the letters change places too

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Someone insists that taking breaks matters to a dancer.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective: 'savvy American' means shrewd, in an American idiom, not a savvy person.
annotation.definitionFit: An American coinage for the shrewdness learned on city streets rather than in school.

entries.clue: Five seen in Christmas story (5)

indicatorNotes.seen in: something seen in a place is inside it, so V sits inside NOEL

blocks.note: Noel is Christmas
V is five in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: Someone spots the number five in a Christmas tale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Christmas story' reads as one phrase, but Christmas is wordplay and 'story' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a book-length work of prose fiction is a story.

entries.clue: Basic tools of hostile criminal (7)

indicatorNotes.criminal: a criminal is bent, crooked, and bent letters are pushed out of their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A description of the crude weapons carried by an aggressive crook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hostile criminal' looks like an adjective and noun; criminal is the anagram signal and hostile the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Crudely chipped flints once taken for the earliest human tools, so tools of the most basic kind.

entries.clue: Run faster than anyone else on final part of lap, correct? (3,3,6,8)

blocks.note: running faster than anyone ever has puts your time in the books
the home straight is the last stretch of a lap

annotation.surface: A question about a runner breaking a record on the home stretch.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue looks like athletics; only the last word, 'correct', is the definition, and it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put right a false account of events is to correct it.

entries.clue: Weirdly, I curtsey for bouncer? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a bouncer is one example of security staff, hence the question mark

indicatorNotes.Weirdly: something done weirdly is done strangely, so the letters come out in a strange order

blocks.note: anagram indicator
anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Someone admits to an odd curtsey offered to the doorman at a club.
annotation.walkthrough: A bouncer is the doorman who keeps out troublemakers at a club or pub; the question mark says he is one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the doorman at a club is part of the staff who keep the place safe.

entries.clue: Attached new structure briefly to support component of wheel (6,3)

indicatorNotes.briefly: a word said briefly is cut short, so FORT loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.to support: in a down clue the lower part holds up the one above, so N FOR sits under SPOKE

blocks.note: a spoke is part of a wheel
N = new
FORT, a structure, cut short

annotation.surface: Instructions for fitting a new part beneath a wheel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attached' looks like assembly language, as in bolted on, but it means in a relationship.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone already in a relationship is taken, attached to a partner.

entries.clue: Henry visits small restaurant for bit of cereal (5)

indicatorNotes.visits: a visitor goes inside the place visited, so Henry's H goes inside the café

blocks.note: a caff is a cheap British café
H = henry, the unit of inductance

annotation.surface: Henry drops in at a café for a bite of breakfast cereal.
annotation.walkthrough: A caff is British slang for a cheap café. The surface wants cereal to be breakfast; it is the grain crop.
annotation.definitionFit: The husks threshed away from wheat or other grain are one part of the cereal plant.

entries.clue: Payments from magnificent matches (9)

blocks.note: royal = magnificent, fit for a king
cup ties are matches

annotation.surface: A football club earns money from some grand fixtures.
annotation.walkthrough: A tie is a knockout match in British football, as in an FA Cup tie.
annotation.definitionFit: Sums paid to an author or rights holder each time a work is sold or used.

entries.clue: Wearing jewellery, returned to island (7)

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: a letter addressed to someone opens with Dear
an ait is a small island in a river

annotation.surface: A bejewelled traveller comes back to an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To island' has to be read as the address on a letter, which would begin 'Dear Ait'. An ait is a small island in a river such as the Thames.
annotation.definitionFit: Wearing a tiara, the jewelled crown-like band, so wearing jewellery of one kind.

entries.clue: Tell school to accept fool (6)

indicatorNotes.to accept: to accept something is to take it in, so SCH takes NIT inside it

blocks.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
a nit is a fool

annotation.surface: Someone is told to report their school for admitting an idiot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tell' is the verb to tell on someone, to inform, not to say.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang for informing on someone, as a child tells on a classmate.

entries.clue: Recalled nut gathering as most poor (7)

indicatorNotes.Recalled: called back, so FAN runs backwards

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fan
a fest is a gathering, as in a beer fest

annotation.surface: Nuts collected in a poor harvest are being recalled.
annotation.walkthrough: Naff is British slang for tacky or poor quality. 'Nut gathering' suggests squirrels; nut is an enthusiast here.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang superlative: the most tacky or shoddy, so the poorest in quality.

entries.clue: Trump picked up seaweed close to major battle site (9)

indicatorNotes.picked up: in a down clue, lifting a word up makes it read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its end, so the last letter of major

blocks.note: trump is British slang for breaking wind
an alga is a seaweed
last letter of major

annotation.surface: A politician collects seaweed near a great battlefield.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants Donald Trump; in British slang to trump is to break wind. 'Major' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The cape off south-west Spain where Nelson beat the French and Spanish fleets in 1805.

entries.clue: Material had rewrites to be edited (6,5)

indicatorNotes.to be edited: editing moves words about, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Some written material needed several rewrites before editing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' pretends to be written copy, which the rewrites and editing support; it is cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: A woollen cloth handwoven in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland, so a material in the fabric sense.

entries.clue: The making of modern America is raw? (13,3)

blocks.note: the straight reading: the conflict that created the United States
the setter's reading: RAW is what you get by turning a three-letter word round, so the answer describes it

annotation.surface: A question whether the founding of modern America was a crude business.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, WAR made revolutionary, turned round, and it produces RAW, which is what the clue shows.
annotation.definitionFit: The 1775 to 1783 war in which the American colonies won independence from Britain.

entries.clue: Attachment on the side and centre of safe light (6)

indicatorNotes.centre of: the centre of a word is its middle letters

blocks.note: middle two letters of sAFe
fair = light, as in fair hair

annotation.surface: A description of a lamp fitted to the side and middle of a safe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attachment on the side' reads as a fitting; it is a romance conducted on the side.
annotation.definitionFit: An extramarital romance: an emotional attachment carried on beside a marriage.

entries.clue: We set such homophones very indiscriminately at the moment of truth (4,4,5,2,5)

indicatorNotes.indiscriminately: things set indiscriminately are put down with no regard for order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 20 letters; very gives V
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A crossword setter confesses to scattering sound-alike clues about at random.
annotation.walkthrough: V is the standard abbreviation for very. 'Homophones' is fodder, not a signal to listen.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for the point when a decision can no longer be put off.

entries.clue: Lie on the counter to receive constant acclaim (5)

indicatorNotes.on the counter: counter means against the usual direction, so TALE runs backwards
indicatorNotes.to receive: to receive something is to take it in, so C goes inside

blocks.note: a tale is a lie, as in telling tales
c is the constant for the speed of light

annotation.surface: A shop assistant fibs at the counter to win praise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a shop counter; it is the reversal signal. C, the speed of light, is a standard constant.
annotation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for brilliant success and the applause that greets it.

entries.clue: Cautious man would add petrol, perhaps, to have energy earlier (7)

indicatorNotes.earlier: earlier means sooner in the sequence, so the E moves forward

blocks.note: he'd = he would
petrol is one kind of fuel, and to fuel is to add it
E = energy; the E of FUEL moves forward, just after HE

annotation.surface: A careful driver says he would fill up first to have power later.
annotation.walkthrough: HE'D FUEL is one letter from the answer: shift its E forward. Petrol is British for gasoline.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: paying careful heed, taking care.

entries.clue: Jew somehow has to know one welcoming extreme characters (9)

indicatorNotes.somehow: done somehow means done in some unstated way, so the letters of has are rearranged
indicatorNotes.welcoming: a host welcoming guests takes them in, so KEN I takes AZ inside it

blocks.note: anagram of has
to ken is to know
I = one
A and Z are the two ends of the alphabet

annotation.surface: Someone must somehow get to know a visitor who welcomes eccentrics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extreme characters' looks like eccentric people; here it is the alphabet's first and last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: The name for Jews of Central and Eastern European descent, one of the main branches of the Jewish people.

entries.clue: Periodically, Spain asks to get rid of repellent type (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Periodically: at regular periods, so take every other letter: SpAiN aSkS
indicatorNotes.repellent: something repellent drives others back, so FIRE runs backwards

blocks.note: alternate letters of SpAiN aSkS
to fire is to get rid of, as a worker

annotation.surface: Every so often Spain asks to be rid of an off-putting kind of person.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Repellent type' reads as an unpleasant person; repellent is the reversal signal and type means typeface.
annotation.definitionFit: A family of typefaces whose letters lack the small finishing strokes called serifs.

entries.clue: Old reactive metal found in new entrance hall (7)

blocks.note: N = new
an atrium is an entrance hall

annotation.surface: A chemical discovered lying about in a newly built lobby.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Found in' looks like a signal to hide something inside; it only links definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The former name for sodium, a highly reactive metal, which is why its symbol is Na.

entries.clue: Smile ahead of fellow’s progress (5,2)

blocks.note: a grin is a smile
a don is a fellow of a college; the 's is 'is', joining to the definition

annotation.surface: A grin foreshadows a colleague's advance.
annotation.walkthrough: A don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for moving forward slowly and relentlessly, a laborious kind of progress.

entries.clue: Ring during post-mortem; morgue upset (7)

indicatorNotes.during: during means within the time of, so the answer lies within the words
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: post-morTEM; MORGue, read backwards

annotation.surface: A ring turns up during an autopsy and the mortuary is in uproar.
annotation.walkthrough: The morbid words are only letters; read backwards through 'mortem; morgue'.
annotation.definitionFit: A rubber or metal ring that lines a hole, so a ring of a practical kind.

entries.clue: Competent drunk (5)

blocks.note: a well-drilled band or crew is said to be this
an old slang word for drunk

annotation.surface: A verdict on someone who is capable despite being inebriated.
annotation.walkthrough: The competent sense is as in 'we run a tight ship', or a band that plays tightly together.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are informal: well drilled and precise, and the old slang for drunk.

entries.clue: While contracted, husband is welcomed by singer (5)

indicatorNotes.is welcomed by: a guest welcomed by a host is taken inside, so H goes inside ALTO

blocks.note: an alto is a singer
H = husband

annotation.surface: During the engagement, the husband-to-be is welcomed by a vocalist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' means shortened: the answer is a clipped although, and although can mean while. The surface makes it a marriage contract.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal short spelling of although, which in 'while I agree' means while.

entries.clue: Conquest stops fantastic snog speedily (2,5)

indicatorNotes.stops: a stopper plugs a gap, so WIN plugs the gap in the other letters
indicatorNotes.fantastic: fantastic means unreal, fanciful, so the letters of snog take a fanciful new order

blocks.note: anagram of snog
a conquest is a win

annotation.surface: A romantic conquest stops a great kiss rather quickly.
annotation.walkthrough: Snog is British slang for a long passionate kiss.
annotation.definitionFit: A poetic idiom: to go as if flying is to go fast.

entries.clue: Plant essential work by little sister (9)

blocks.note: core = essential, as in core subjects
OP is short for opus, a work
sis is a shortened sister

annotation.surface: A reminder that the vital gardening was done by a younger sister.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb telling you to plant something; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A daisy-like garden flower, often yellow, also called tickseed.

entries.clue: Rest of lake going into Ouse, it’s said (5)

indicatorNotes.going into: something going into another ends up inside it, so L goes inside
indicatorNotes.it’s said: said aloud, so Ouse is heard as ooze

blocks.note: Ouse sounds like ooze, and to ooze is to seep
L = lake

annotation.surface: Water from a lake flows into the River Ouse.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in England, said like ooze; the synonym seep then takes the L.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the body's nightly rest.

entries.clue: They deliver and drive growth (7)

blocks.note: UPS, the parcel company, delivers
an urge is a drive

annotation.surface: A courier firm's slogan about delivering and driving the economy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'They' is the parcel firm UPS; 'drive' is a noun, as in sex drive.
annotation.definitionFit: A sudden rise or increase, a burst of growth.

entries.clue: Less drunk, retrospectively screen missing diamonds for bishop (7)

indicatorNotes.retrospectively: retrospect is looking back, so the word is read backwards
indicatorNotes.missing: a missing thing is absent, so the D goes
indicatorNotes.for: one thing for another means in its place, so B takes the D's place

blocks.note: a reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar
D = diamonds, the card suit; it leaves
B = bishop in chess; the swap leaves REREBOS

annotation.surface: Someone sobering up looks back at a screen missing some diamonds.
annotation.walkthrough: The key is the church word REREDOS; swap its D for B and read REREBOS from the end.
annotation.definitionFit: The comparative of sober: further from drunkenness.

entries.clue: Triggers people sampling flagellation, according to Spooner (9)

indicatorNotes.according to Spooner: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: flagellation is whipping; WHIP takes the TR sound from the next word
people sampling something are triers; TRIERS takes the WH sound in exchange

annotation.surface: Something that sets off people experimenting with the lash.
annotation.walkthrough: Swap the WH and TR sounds of WHIP TRIERS.
annotation.definitionFit: Wires stretched low that set off a trap, bomb or alarm when disturbed, so devices that trigger.

entries.clue: Fight a bit (5)

blocks.note: informal for a brawl or scuffle
a small leftover piece, as of paper

annotation.surface: An admission of fighting a little.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'a bit' as a noun, a fragment, not as 'slightly'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are nouns: an informal word for a fight, and a small leftover piece.

entries.clue: Station surrounded by multitude of buses ignoring old lady with hungry dog (6,7)

indicatorNotes.surrounded by: HUB is surrounded by the other letters
indicatorNotes.ignoring: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the O is dropped

blocks.note: a computer's main circuit board carries many buses, the lines that carry data
O = old, dropped from MOTHERBOARD
a hub is a station, as in a transport hub

annotation.surface: A bus station scene, with an elderly woman and a starving dog.
annotation.walkthrough: Buses here are computer circuits, not vehicles. 'Old' also looks like part of 'old lady'; it is the dropped O.
annotation.definitionFit: The nursery-rhyme woman who went to the cupboard for a bone and found it bare, so her poor dog had none.

entries.clue: Work to protect old city with millions in trouble (7)

indicatorNotes.to protect: a protector wraps around what it guards, so TOIL wraps round UR and M

blocks.note: toil is work
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
M = millions

annotation.surface: Efforts to defend an ancient city with a fortune fail in chaos.
annotation.walkthrough: Ur, in ancient Mesopotamia, is the crossword's standard old city.
annotation.definitionFit: A state of great disturbance and confusion, trouble in its widest sense.

entries.clue: Bedlam at Eurovision entertains enthusiast (7)

indicatorNotes.entertains: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so the phrase holds the answer within it

blocks.note: bedlAM AT EURovision

annotation.surface: Chaos at the Eurovision Song Contest delights a fan.
annotation.walkthrough: Eurovision is the annual European song contest, famous for its chaos.
annotation.definitionFit: From Latin amator, a lover: someone who does a thing for love of it rather than pay.

entries.clue: Fuss around small guitar beginning to rile manager (13)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: ado is fuss
mini = small
a Strat is a Fender Stratocaster guitar
first letter of rile

annotation.surface: A fuss over a little guitar begins to annoy the boss.
annotation.walkthrough: The Fender Stratocaster is known to players simply as a Strat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: one who runs the affairs of an office or organisation.

entries.clue: A group playing popular covers start to shout “Get out while you can!” (7,4)

indicatorNotes.covers: a cover goes over and around what it covers, so HIP goes around S
indicatorNotes.start to: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: A as written
a band is a musical group
on = playing, as in on stage
first letter of shout
hip = fashionable, popular; it covers the S

annotation.surface: A band plays pop covers before someone yells at the crowd to flee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covers' suggests cover versions of songs; it is a verb, telling one piece to wrap round another.
annotation.definitionFit: The order to get off a sinking vessel while there is still time.

entries.clue: Able to produce young almost immediately, taking care when cavorting (9)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost the whole word, so PRONTO loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.taking: to take something in is to contain it, so PRONT takes the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.when cavorting: cavorting is leaping about, so the letters of care leap into a new order

blocks.note: PRONTO, immediately, almost complete
anagram of care

annotation.surface: Animals that can breed almost at once are careful when frolicking.
annotation.walkthrough: PRONTO is informal for immediately; its last letter goes before the anagram is tucked in after PRO.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare adjective from procreate: capable of begetting offspring.

entries.clue: Doctor nearly agreed to break glass appliance (6,5)

indicatorNotes.nearly: nearly all of a word, so YES loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.to break: to break something is to split it open, so DR YE splits TUMBLER

blocks.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass
DR = doctor
YES, agreed, nearly complete

annotation.surface: A doctor almost consented to smashing a glass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Glass appliance' looks like a unit; glass is the wordplay and appliance alone the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A household machine that dries laundry in a heated rotating drum.

entries.clue: Mentor drives a buggy (7)

indicatorNotes.buggy: buggy software is faulty, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A mentor takes the wheel of a small cart.
annotation.walkthrough: Buggy is a vehicle in the surface and the anagram signal in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trusted guide who gives counsel.

entries.clue: Investigative team deputy’s motor vehicle (4,5)

blocks.note: a vice is a deputy, as in vice-president; VICE'S
a quad is a quad bike, a four-wheeled motor vehicle

annotation.surface: A police unit uses the deputy's car.
annotation.walkthrough: Vice as a noun means a deputy; the 's joins it to the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: The police unit that investigates crimes such as prostitution, drugs and gambling.

entries.clue: Maybe it starts to cause enmity, say (9)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: the word it is one example of this part of speech
first letters of cause and enmity

annotation.surface: A remark that something might be the start of bad blood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' is not a vague thing but the word it, and 'maybe' marks it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to utter a word, or to declare aloud.

entries.clue: Switch positions to suppress outspoken notices when business is slow (3,6)

indicatorNotes.to suppress: to suppress is to hold down and keep in, so OFF ON keeps the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.outspoken: spoken out, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: a switch has two positions
notices = sees, which sounds like seas

annotation.surface: Staff switch jobs to hide candid notices while trade is quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Switch positions' looks like a job swap; it is the two settings of a light switch.
annotation.definitionFit: The quiet months of a resort or trade, when custom falls away.

entries.clue: Cage, perhaps, reportedly containing metal (9)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: as reported by word of mouth, so the name is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: the actor Nicolas Cage; his first name is what you hear

annotation.surface: A cage said to hold metal.
annotation.walkthrough: Cage is the actor Nicolas Cage, and 'perhaps' says he is one example of a Nicolas.
annotation.definitionFit: A chemist's adjective for compounds holding nickel, a metal.

entries.clue: Ambassador covered in strange nasal discharge (5)

indicatorNotes.covered in: a thing covered in something is wrapped in it, so HE is wrapped in RUM

blocks.note: rum = strange, odd
HE = His Excellency, an ambassador's title

annotation.surface: A diplomat is spattered with some odd mucus.
annotation.walkthrough: Rum is old British slang for odd. An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, HE.
annotation.definitionFit: An old word for the watery fluid that runs from the nose and eyes.

entries.clue: Oblivious about introduction of cream in coffee (5)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so DEAF goes around C
indicatorNotes.introduction of: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: deaf = oblivious, as in deaf to advice
first letter of cream

annotation.surface: Someone does not notice cream being added to their coffee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' is the link, not a container signal; 'about' does that work.
annotation.definitionFit: Short for decaffeinated coffee, the kind with the caffeine removed.

entries.clue: Female to entice inspiring former partner in turn (7)

indicatorNotes.inspiring: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes in the other

blocks.note: F = female
to lure is to entice
an ex is a former partner

annotation.surface: A woman lures back her ex, taking her turn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inspiring' looks like praise for the ex; read it literally as breathing in.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical word for a bend or curve, so a turn in the shape of something.

entries.clue: Country cops following archangel (7)

indicatorNotes.cops: to cop is to catch, so the country catches F and holds it

blocks.note: Israel is a country
F = following, as in pp. 5f.

annotation.surface: A nation's police follow an angel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cops' is a verb meaning catches, not police.
annotation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition, the archangel who will sound the trumpet on the Day of Judgement.

entries.clue: I’m surprised time interrupts count again (7)

indicatorNotes.interrupts: to interrupt is to break into, so T breaks into the exclamation

blocks.note: Really! is what you say when surprised
T = time

annotation.surface: A surprised official stops the clock to count the votes again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I'm surprised' stands for a one-word exclamation of surprise.
annotation.definitionFit: A prefixed verb: a tally is a count, and the prefix re- adds the again.

entries.clue: Irishman drinks red liquid in church (9)

indicatorNotes.drinks: a drinker takes liquid in, so CATHAL takes the other letters inside
indicatorNotes.liquid: liquid flows and has no fixed shape, so the letters flow into a new order

blocks.note: Cathal is an Irish man's name
anagram of red

annotation.surface: An Irishman sips red wine inside a church.
annotation.walkthrough: Cathal is a common Irish first name; 'red liquid' suggests wine, but liquid is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: The principal church of a diocese, seat of its bishop.

entries.clue: Burst in and blushed, having forgotten wife takes ecstasy (7)

indicatorNotes.having forgotten: what is forgotten is left out, so the W is dropped
indicatorNotes.takes: to take something in is to hold it, so the remainder takes E inside

blocks.note: to blush is to go red: went red
W = wife, dropped
E = ecstasy, the drug

annotation.surface: A man burst in and went red, having left his wife, high on drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: Blushed has to be expanded into two words, WENT RED, before anything can be removed.
annotation.definitionFit: Bursting in is a forceful way of going in, and the past tense matches.

entries.clue: Shelter from sunshine, suffering with temperature (6,3)

indicatorNotes.suffering: something suffering is in a bad way, knocked about, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
anagram indicator
T = temperature, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone seeks cover from the sun because of a fever.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is a British prefabricated corrugated-iron hut from the First World War, like an American Quonset hut.
annotation.definitionFit: A half-cylinder of corrugated iron used for troops and stores, a shelter of the plainest kind.

entries.clue: Fast, say (7)

blocks.note: high-speed, as a train or delivery that makes no stops
to put into words

annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example'; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective for high-speed service and a verb for putting thoughts into words.

entries.clue: Singer? Just beat it! (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the question mark signals that the singer is a songbird

blocks.note: to pip is to beat narrowly
it as written

annotation.surface: Someone tells a performer to get lost.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beat it' looks like 'go away', but the split falls between beat and it. To be pipped at the post is British for being narrowly beaten.
annotation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird of fields and moors, so a singer in the bird sense.

entries.clue: In rows, leading European leaves exhausted (5)

indicatorNotes.leaves: to leave is to go away, so the E goes from the word

blocks.note: tiered = arranged in rows, like seats
the first letter of European, E, departs

annotation.surface: A European front-runner walks off, worn out, from a crowd in rows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like foliage but is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: worn out and in need of rest.

entries.clue: More fully developed American departing to make amends for going north (5)

indicatorNotes.departing: someone departing goes away, so the A goes from the word
indicatorNotes.going north: north is up the page, so in a down clue the word reads upwards, backwards

blocks.note: to repair a wrong is to make amends for it
A = American, removed to leave REPIR
